clue.text: Hang around cloister chapter and Saint have left

indicators.note: the chapter and saint letters are said to depart, so they are taken out of the word cloister

explanation.surface: A monk lingers in the cloister after the chapter meeting and the saint have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C and S out of CLOISTER, leaving LOITER.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly in one place, which is what hanging around means.

clue.text: Destructive insect — place has tons

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

explanation.surface: A pest arrives in huge numbers at some spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are grasshoppers whose swarms strip crops bare, the classic ruinous insect.

clue.text: Lunatic or amusing fool?

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of the words that follow are jumbled wildly

explanation.surface: Is a madcap or comic person just a fool?
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant, foolish person, a dunce.

clue.text: Each evening going on railway

parts.note: eve is a poetic word for evening

explanation.surface: Every night someone travels by train.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every are near synonyms, both meaning all members of a group taken singly.

clue.text: Hitchin caller regularly observed hard water in winter

indicators.note: only letters at regular intervals in these words are looked at, every second one

explanation.surface: Someone phoning from Hitchin, a Hertfordshire town, kept noticing the frozen water.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of HITCHIN CALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is frozen, solid water hanging from eaves in cold weather, a playful description.

clue.text: Wine with tea, not quite the greatest joy

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: the word is not quite finished, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: bliss is the greatest joy

explanation.surface: Pairing a drink of wine with tea isn't the height of pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final S; cha is British slang for tea, as in 'a cup of cha'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from northern Burgundy in France.

clue.text: Greek character's cold greeting

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A Greek person gives a frosty hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: One third of twelve — not odd number

indicators.note: the six-letter word twelve split into thirds, and the central third of it is taken

parts.note: a number that is not odd is even

explanation.surface: A puzzling arithmetic statement about dividing twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle third of TWELVE is EL; add EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a whole number, the one after ten.

clue.text: Thinking of confusing VAT incomplete

indicators.note: confusing letters mixes them up, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is brooding over unfinished, baffling value added tax forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A contemplative person is thoughtful, given to deep reflection.

clue.text: Power or oil frequently turned up in list of investments

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses these words so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: Energy or oil shares often appear in an investor's holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads the reversed pair from bottom to top, giving TFOLIO; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is the set of investments held by one person or fund.

clue.text: Apologetic with small truck not starting

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: the word does not start, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: a lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: A driver says sorry because the little truck won't start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry means feeling regret, full of apology.

clue.text: Turning paler, intitially suffer extreme return to bad health

indicators.note: turning the letters over and around rearranges them
the clue's misspelling of initially: the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A patient going pale at first suffers badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges PALER to give RELAP; add SE from the starts of suffer and extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is the return of illness after an apparent recovery, a slide back into sickness.

clue.text: Utter professional has word with civil engineer

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a noun is a kind of word

explanation.surface: An expert has a quiet word with an engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to speak or say a word aloud, to utter it.

clue.text: Aims often broken?

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that stated aims are frequently not kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a wry description: a political party's manifesto sets out its aims, which are famously often broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public declaration of policy and intentions, notably at elections.

clue.text: No bridge partners surpass uninterruptedly

parts.note: North and South are partners at the card game bridge
to top is to surpass

explanation.surface: Card partners without a break keep beating everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonstop as an adverb means without a pause or interruption, continuously.

clue.text: Pet frightens with head right down

indicators.note: the first letter is moved all the way down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: scares means frightens

explanation.surface: A pet animal scares people by lowering its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial S of SCARES goes to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet an animal is to stroke it fondly, a caress; pet is a verb here.

clue.text: Hit with a band

definitions.meaning: struck hard, past tense of belt
... also describes something fitted with a belt or encircled by a stripe

explanation.definitionFit: Belt as a verb means to thump, and belted as an adjective means wearing or marked by a belt.

clue.text: Stadium housing second Lima football team

indicators.note: the stadium contains, houses, the next letter

parts.note: an arena is a stadium
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A stadium is hosting a second team from Lima in Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside ARENA, then L follows. Arsenal is a London Premier League football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous English football club based in north London.

clue.text: Diamond perhaps with slight, not light, colour

indicators.note: the word light is excluded from slight, leaving only the first letter

parts.note: a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A gem has a faint, rather dark tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight, not light' leaves S; add TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is an example of a precious stone, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: A lot of insects needing southern heat

parts.note: to warm is to heat

explanation.surface: Many insects need the warmth of the south to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large mass of insects, such as bees, moving together.

clue.text: What has metal core working with good capture?

definitions.text: What has metal core working with good capture?

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to net is to capture

explanation.surface: A riddle about a device whose iron core does well at picking things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges METAL CORE to ELECTROMA; add G and NET. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a magnet with an iron core that picks up metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An electromagnet is a coil wound around an iron core that becomes magnetic when current flows, attracting iron.

clue.text: A long time shut up in seraglio

indicators.note: the answer is enclosed, locked inside the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone spent ages confined in a harem.
explanation.walkthrough: A seraglio is a harem, the women's quarters of an Ottoman palace.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history.

clue.text: Swindle with pie lacking English seafood

parts.note: a scam is a swindle

indicators.note: the word is lacking the following letter, so it is removed

explanation.surface: A con involving a pie with no English food in it, only seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a pub favourite in Britain.

clue.text: Loom I repair without pressure

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the repair word goes around the next letter

parts.note: to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fix a weaving loom without any stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so MEND wraps P.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to be about to happen, to hang threateningly over, as a storm looms.
